note:
Marrow Street’s anchor and the only thing on that strip with four floors. A department store sets
BACK rather than twists — three diminishing storeys over a deep shopfront podium, a centred
chamfered attic and the corner rotunda on top, which is what a store of this kind actually puts
there.

⚠ THE SETBACKS WERE ALWAYS THERE AND NOBODY COULD SEE THEM, which is what a single palette does
to a wedding cake: 0.44 → 0.41 → 0.33 → 0.24 and a rotunda, every step of it the same brown, so
four storeys of massing read as one lump. `models:quality` scores "more than one wall palette"
for exactly this. It has three now — cast stone round the shopfront and across the attic,
soot-darkened brick for the base course and the rotunda, and the sodium brown kept for the shaft,
which is the one that had to stay.

⚠ ITS NEON STAYS SODIUM ON PURPOSE. Everything west of here burns magenta or cyan now; this is
the middle of the gradient, and the warm sign is how the street says so without a coordinate
being named anywhere in the renderer.

⚠ THE SHOPFRONT IS THE BUILDING’S SUBJECT AND IT WAS A STRIP. The zone calls it "a wall of
mannequins in this season’s one coat", and a wall is what it has to be: one continuous glazed
band the full width of the podium, nine lights of it, under a canopy that reaches the kerb. The
old one was 0.045 of the height at seven bars and read as a row of vents.

⚠ A CANTILEVER AND A ROTATION NEVER SHARE A SEGMENT — see the warning in aurelia.json. An offset
box and a yawed box are each safe; a box that is both puts the derived kit where its own solid is
not, and glself catches it. So asymmetry here is offset-only and every chamfer is CENTRED.
RENDER_TUNE.legacyArms puts the deptstore arm back.

⚠ THE ROOF BOARD IS AUTHORED SO THAT IT DOES NOT SAY THE NAME TWICE. `derivedKit` hands this
building a rooftop hoarding on 25 seeds in 40 and labels it off the building, which put ADEQUATE!
on the fascia and ADEQUATE! on the roof. A store this size should have a roof sign; what it should
not have is the same word on both. The slogan is the store’s own joke and tells a player
something the fascia does not.

⚠ THE SIGN STAYS SODIUM AND THE GLASS DOES NOT, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE.
Every window on the building took `glass: #1c1712` — a near-black brown — so by day a four-storey
store was a tan box with black slots in it, and after dark all four floors burned the same warm
cream as the fascia. That is the whole city being amber inside one building. A window reflects the
SKY, so the day colour is cool slate and the night one is a cool white-blue, colder again on the
top floor. The name still burns sodium, and it is the only thing that does.

⚠ THE DISPLAY IS MAGENTA BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE SURFACE HERE LIT TO BE LOOKED AT. "A wall of
mannequins in this season’s one coat" is not room light behind glass, it is a shop window on
a timer, and the city rule is that the field goes cool and the hot colour is spent on the thing
that earns it. Nine lights of it under the canopy, with the pavement pool to match and the sodium
one moved across to the door.

⚠ AND THE PODIUM HAS A LIT CORNICE. The setbacks are the building’s argument and at night the
podium and the shaft were one dark mass with a sign stuck on it; a cyan tube under the stone
parapet draws the line the massing already has. It claims the `neon` section, so the derived kit
stays off this facade rather than hanging a second one somewhere it was not designed for.
